current.text: Houston's guard rotation is crowded. Fred VanVleet is back, and the Rockets added Marcus Smart and Bogdan Bogdanovic.
Coach Ime Udoka blamed Sheppard for defensive mistakes and pulls him quickly when he makes them. Udoka has played Josh Okogie ahead of him.
Several experts think Udoka dislikes Sheppard and will not change his mind.

Experts project him off the bench. The projected starters are VanVleet, Amen Thompson, Kevin Durant, Jabari Smith Jr. and Alperen Sengun. Thompson and Smart could take most of the point guard minutes, and he may not even make the top eight of the rotation.
Lloyd projects about 26 minutes a night but says Sheppard may struggle to match last season's minutes. Experts expect him to take a step back this season.
His minutes should swing from game to game. He will play more when he is hot from three.
If he got a 28 to 30 minute starting role, he could be a top 40 to top 50 player. The experts do not expect that role without big injuries.

His 29th to 30th place in season-total nine-category rankings is misleading. It comes from playing 82 games. He was 93rd in head-to-head value, and 129th before the trade deadline against 45th after it.
Draft him only as a cheap late upside flier. Josh values him at 1 USD (he went for 5 USD in a mock). Lloyd doubts he breaks the top 100 and sees him as a round-10 swing around pick 110 to 120.
His ESPN rank near 58 is far too high. Lloyd calls him his biggest fade on ESPN.
With a March 28 end, Houston has a weak 3-3-4 fantasy playoff schedule, 10 games over weeks 19 to 21.
Houston has only 14 back-to-backs this season.

durable.text: He has a strong category profile: many threes on good three-point shooting, high steals and blocks for a guard, solid assists and good free throw shooting on low volume.
He is worth more in category leagues than in points leagues.
He is small and struggles on defense. He picks up his dribble too often and is too soft with the ball, so he needs to get stronger.

note: Sheppard has a real category profile: 2.7 threes and 1.5 steals projected. But the experts agree his role shrinks behind VanVleet, Smart and Bogdanovic under a coach who distrusts him. In our league he is a 1 to 5 USD late flier. Pay closer to Yahoo's 1 USD (rank 141) than ESPN's 7 USD (rank 62), and below the 4 USD our league paid last season. Early in the season, check whether he stays in the top eight of the rotation and gets 25 or more minutes. Watch for any guard injury that could open a starting role. Note too that Houston's 10-game playoff schedule is weak.
